claim: Analysis of the spatial distribution of endomembrane trafficking is fundamental to understand the mechanisms controlling cellular dynamics, cell homeostasy, and cell interaction with its external environment in normal and pathological situations.
source: Analysis of the spatial distribution of endomembrane trafficking is fundamental to understand the mechanisms controlling cellular dynamics, cell homeostasy, and cell interaction with its external environment in normal and pathological situations.
evidence: This is a statement about the importance of spatial distribution analysis, drawing from established scientific knowledge about cellular mechanisms.

claim: QuantEv automatically estimates weighted densities that are easy to interpret from the spatial coordinates of intracellular features.
source: From the spatial coordinates of intracellular features such as segmented subcellular structures or vesicle trajectories, QuantEv automatically estimates weighted densities that are easy to interpret and performs a comprehensive statistical analysis from distribution distances.
evidence: This describes the computational method developed in this study.

claim: QuantEv performs a comprehensive statistical analysis from distribution distances.
source: From the spatial coordinates of intracellular features such as segmented subcellular structures or vesicle trajectories, QuantEv automatically estimates weighted densities that are easy to interpret and performs a comprehensive statistical analysis from distribution distances.
evidence: This describes the statistical analysis capability of the method.

claim: Most computational methods for analyzing fluorescent images are based on the complex combination of heterogeneous features which makes it difficult to draw definitive biological conclusions.
source: However, most computational methods are based on the complex combination of heterogeneous features such as statistical, geometrical, morphological and frequency properties (Peng, 2008), which makes it difficult to draw definitive biological conclusions.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Most experimental designs at single-cell level pool together data coming from replicated experiments of a given condition, neglecting the biological variability between individual cells.
source: Additionally, most experimental designs, especially at single-cell level, pool together data coming from replicated experiments of a given condition (Schauer et al., 2010; Merouane et al., 2015; Biot et al., 2016), neglecting the biological variability between individual cells.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Micro-patterning is a well-established strategy to reduce morphological variability by imposing constraints on adhesion sites.
source: Micro-patterning is now a well-established strategy to reduce morphological variability by imposing constraints on adhesion sites, which has been shown to influence the cytoskeleton geometry and transport carrier localization (Théry et al., 2005; Schauer et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Micro-patterning has been shown to influence the cytoskeleton geometry and transport carrier localization.
source: Micro-patterning is now a well-established strategy to reduce morphological variability by imposing constraints on adhesion sites, which has been shown to influence the cytoskeleton geometry and transport carrier localization (Théry et al., 2005; Schauer et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The kernel density-based test does not consider the sample-to-sample variability because all replicated experiments from a given condition are simply merged together.
source: Unfortunately, it does not consider the sample-to-sample variability because all replicated experiments from a given condition are simply merged together.
evidence: This is a critique of existing methods based on logical inference.

claim: QuantEv uses the Earth Mover's Distance and the Circular Earth Mover's Distance to measure the dissimilarity between densities associated with different experimental conditions.
source: We use the Earth Mover's Distance (Rubner et al., 2000) and the Circular Earth Mover's Distance (Rabin et al., 2011) to measure the dissimilarity between densities associated with different experimental conditions.
evidence: This describes the distance metrics used, with citations to the original methods.

claim: QuantEv identifies the point that gives the most uniform angular distribution, which may coincide with a biological structure of interest that would act as the events emitter or attractor.
source: By computing weighted densities for each point in the cell as the reference center, QuantEv identifies the point that gives the most uniform angular distribution. This point may coincide with a biological structure of interest that would act as the events emitter or attractor.
evidence: This describes a capability of the method and speculates about its biological interpretation.

claim: Rab6 proteins are transiently anchored to moving transport carriers from the Golgi apparatus located at the cell center to Endoplasmic Reticulum entry sites or to plasma membrane.
source: Rab6 proteins are transiently anchored to moving transport carriers from the Golgi apparatus located at the cell center to Endoplasmic Reticulum entry sites or to plasma membrane (White et al., 1999; Chavrier and Goud, 1999; Echard et al., 2000; Opdam et al., 2000; Grigoriev et al., 2007; Bardin et al., 2015), both assumed to be located at the cell periphery.
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous work.

claim: Cell shape imposes constraints on the cytoskeleton and consequently influences the spatial distribution of Rab6 transport carriers.
source: Cell shape imposes constraints on the cytoskeleton and consequently influences the spatial distribution of Rab6 transport carriers, as confirmed with kernel density maps (Schauer et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Rab6 positive membranes were reported to move from and toward the Golgi in apparent close proportions.
source: In addition, Rab6 positive membranes were reported to move from and toward the Golgi in apparent close proportions (Grigoriev et al., 2007, Grigoriev et al., 2011), and yet these membrane associated proteins are believed to traffic in majority from the Golgi located at the cell center to the cell periphery (White et al., 1999; Chavrier and Goud, 1999; Echard et al., 2000; Opdam et al., 2000; Grigoriev et al., 2007) where they should dissociate from membranes and recycle back to the cytosol.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Rab6 membrane associated proteins are believed to traffic in majority from the Golgi located at the cell center to the cell periphery where they should dissociate from membranes and recycle back to the cytosol.
source: In addition, Rab6 positive membranes were reported to move from and toward the Golgi in apparent close proportions (Grigoriev et al., 2007, Grigoriev et al., 2011), and yet these membrane associated proteins are believed to traffic in majority from the Golgi located at the cell center to the cell periphery (White et al., 1999; Chavrier and Goud, 1999; Echard et al., 2000; Opdam et al., 2000; Grigoriev et al., 2007) where they should dissociate from membranes and recycle back to the cytosol.
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous work.

claim: Rab11 is known to be primarily localized to the Endosomal Recycling Compartment (ERC).
source: Rab11 is known to be primarily localized to the Endosomal Recycling Compartment (ERC), and it organizes spatially and temporally recycling from this compartment (Ullrich et al., 1996; Gidon et al., 2012; Baetz and Goldenring, 2013; Boulanger et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Rab11 organizes spatially and temporally recycling from the Endosomal Recycling Compartment.
source: Rab11 is known to be primarily localized to the Endosomal Recycling Compartment (ERC), and it organizes spatially and temporally recycling from this compartment (Ullrich et al., 1996; Gidon et al., 2012; Baetz and Goldenring, 2013; Boulanger et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The KD approach concludes that the distribution of Rab6-positive membranes are clearly different between cells of different shapes with p value = 0.
source: The KD approach concludes that the distribution of Rab6-positive membranes are clearly different between cells of different shapes (see Figure 2a–c, p value = 0 when considering unconstrained cells versus crossbow-shaped cells, unconstrained cells versus disk-shaped cells, and crossbow-shaped cells versus disk-shaped cells).
evidence: This is based on data analysis shown in Figure 2.

claim: The KD approach leads to a significant difference when image sequences with the same cell shape are compared.
source: Unfortunately, it also leads to a significant difference when image sequences with the same cell shape are compared (see Figure 2d).
evidence: This is based on data shown in Figure 2d.

claim: The KD approach is too sensitive.
source: This demonstrates that the KD approach is too sensitive.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation that KD shows differences even for same-shape cells.

claim: QuantEv shows a uniform range of p values when cells with same shape are compared.
source: Instead, QuantEv shows a uniform range of p values when cells with same shape are compared (see Figure 2d) while it leads to significant differences between radial, angular and in-depth distributions of Rab6 proteins from cells with different cell shapes (see Figure 2e–f).
evidence: This is based on data shown in Figure 2d.

claim: QuantEv leads to significant differences between radial, angular and in-depth distributions of Rab6 proteins from cells with different cell shapes.
source: Instead, QuantEv shows a uniform range of p values when cells with same shape are compared (see Figure 2d) while it leads to significant differences between radial, angular and in-depth distributions of Rab6 proteins from cells with different cell shapes (see Figure 2e–f).
evidence: This is based on data shown in Figures 2e-f.

claim: The angular distribution of Rab6 proteins is different for the three cell shapes.
source: The angular distribution of Rab6 proteins is different for the three cell shapes.
evidence: This is based on the analysis results.

claim: The angular distribution of Rab6 proteins ranges from a completely uniform distribution for disk-shaped cells, to a less regular distribution for unconstrained cells and to a distribution oriented toward the three tips of the crossbow for crossbow-shaped cells.
source: It ranges from a completely uniform distribution for disk-shaped cells, to a less regular distribution for unconstrained cells and to a distribution oriented toward the three tips of the crossbow for crossbow-shaped cells.
evidence: This describes the observed patterns in the data.

claim: In-depth and radial distributions are similar for crossbow- and disk-shaped cells.
source: In-depth and radial distributions are similar for crossbow- and disk-shaped cells.
evidence: This is based on the analysis results.

claim: In-depth and radial distributions are different from unconstrained cells compared to constrained cells.
source: In contrast, they are different from unconstrained cells.
evidence: This is based on the analysis results.

claim: Unconstrained cells show diverse sizes with a strong tendency to spread.
source: Unconstrained cells show diverse sizes with a strong tendency to spread.
evidence: This is an observation from the data.

claim: The in-depth distribution is flatter for the unconstrained cells than for the constrained cells because unconstrained cells show diverse sizes with a strong tendency to spread.
source: This explains why the in-depth distribution is flatter for the unconstrained cells than for the constrained cells.
evidence: This is an inference connecting cell spreading to distribution patterns.

claim: QuantEv highlights a distribution maximum for a radius at the two-thirds the distance between the Golgi region border and the cell periphery for both micro-patterns.
source: QuantEv also highlights a distribution maximum for a radius at the two-thirds (resp. five-sixth) the distance between the Golgi region border and the cell periphery for both micro-patterns (resp. unconstrained cells) (see Figure 2f–i).
evidence: This is based on data shown in Figures 2f-i.

claim: QuantEv highlights a distribution maximum for a radius at the five-sixth the distance between the Golgi region border and the cell periphery for unconstrained cells.
source: QuantEv also highlights a distribution maximum for a radius at the two-thirds (resp. five-sixth) the distance between the Golgi region border and the cell periphery for both micro-patterns (resp. unconstrained cells) (see Figure 2f–i).
evidence: This is based on data shown in Figures 2f-i.

claim: The distribution maxima correspond to an accumulation of Rab6-positive membranes and identify the area where they enter a docking phase before switching to a tethering phase.
source: These maxima correspond to an accumulation of Rab6-positive membranes and identify the area where they enter a docking phase before switching to a tethering phase.
evidence: This is a biological interpretation of the observed distribution maxima.

claim: The localization difference for distribution maxima between constrained and unconstrained cells is explained by a smaller adhesion area without micro-patterns, pushing the docking phase for vesicles closer to the cell periphery.
source: The localization difference for these maxima between constrained and unconstrained cells is explained by a smaller adhesion area without micro-patterns, pushing the docking phase for vesicles closer to the cell periphery.
evidence: This is an inference connecting adhesion area to vesicle docking location.

claim: Both radial and angular distributions unraveled by QuantEv represent a measurement of the environment constraints undergone by living cells.
source: Both radial and angular distributions unraveled by QuantEv represent a measurement of the environment constraints undergone by living cells.
evidence: This is an interpretation of what the distributions represent biologically.

claim: The proportion of Rab6-positive membranes moving toward the cell periphery and toward the Golgi are close (0.531 versus 0.469 for unconstrained cells, 0.497 versus 0.503 for crossbow-shaped cells, 0.521 versus 0.479 for disk-shaped cells).
source: As shown in Figure 3d–f, the proportion of Rab6-positive membranes moving toward the cell periphery and toward the Golgi are close (0.531 versus 0.469 for unconstrained cells, 0.497 versus 0.503 for crossbow-shaped cells, 0.521 versus 0.479 for disk-shaped cells).
evidence: This is based on quantitative data shown in Figure 3d-f.

claim: The radial distributions display two distinctive modes for vesicles moving toward the cell periphery and those moving toward the Golgi (p value = 0.0002 for unconstrained cells, p value = 0.021 for crossbow-shaped cells, p value = 0.0008 for disk-shaped cells).
source: However, the radial distributions shown in Figure 3d–f display two distinctive modes for vesicles moving toward the cell periphery and those moving toward the Golgi (p value = 0.0002 for unconstrained cells, p value = 0.021 for crossbow-shaped cells, p value = 0.0008 for disk-shaped cells).
evidence: This is based on statistical analysis of data shown in Figure 3d-f.

claim: Between the Golgi and the distribution maxima, Rab6 vesicles are predominantly moving toward the cell periphery.
source: Between the Golgi and the distribution maxima shown in Figure 2f, Rab6 vesicles are predominantly moving toward the cell periphery.
evidence: This is based on analysis of the spatial distribution data.

claim: Between the distribution maxima and the cell periphery, Rab6 vesicles are in majority moving toward the Golgi.
source: Between these maxima and the cell periphery, they are in majority moving toward the Golgi, indicating that during their docking-tethering phase, the vesicles are predominantly moving toward the cell center.
evidence: This is based on analysis of the spatial distribution data.

claim: During their docking-tethering phase, the Rab6 vesicles are predominantly moving toward the cell center.
source: Between these maxima and the cell periphery, they are in majority moving toward the Golgi, indicating that during their docking-tethering phase, the vesicles are predominantly moving toward the cell center.
evidence: This is an inference from the directional movement data.

claim: The two distinctive dynamical behaviors of Rab6 vesicles are consistent with the aforementioned antagonist statements about bidirectional movement.
source: These two distinctive dynamical behaviors are consistent with the aforementioned antagonist statements.
evidence: This is an inference connecting the observed behaviors to previous literature.

claim: Rab6-positive membranes moving toward the cell periphery have a much more direct path than the ones moving toward the Golgi, except near the cell periphery.
source: Rab6-positive membranes moving toward the cell periphery have a much more direct path than the ones moving toward the Golgi, except near the cell periphery (see Figure 4b, e).
evidence: This is based on confinement ratio data shown in Figure 4b, e.

claim: Rab6 positive membranes moving toward the Golgi have longer total path length and lifetime than the ones moving toward the cell periphery, especially when approaching the cell periphery.
source: Consistently, Rab6 positive membranes moving toward the Golgi have longer total path length and lifetime than the ones moving toward the cell periphery, especially when approaching the cell periphery (see Figure 4c–e).
evidence: This is based on data shown in Figure 4c-e.

claim: Rab6-positive membranes move predominantly and quite directly from the Golgi to the cell periphery until they enter a docking phase, then they mostly go back toward the cell center by following long and indirect trajectories.
source: In summary, this analysis clearly demonstrated that Rab6-positive membranes move predominantly and quite directly from the Golgi to the cell periphery until they enter a docking phase. Then, they mostly go back toward the cell center by following long and indirect trajectories.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the trajectory analysis data.

claim: The point that gives the most uniform angular distribution is close to the manually identified ERC for all image sequences except one.
source: Interestingly, the blue disk is close to the red disk for all image sequences except one (second line, middle image in Figure 5a).
evidence: This is based on visual comparison shown in Figure 5a.

claim: The point that gives the most uniform angular distribution is closer to the manually identified ERC than the cell center in seven out of eight image sequences.
source: The blue disk is also closer to the red disk than the green disk in seven out of eight image sequences (see Figure 5a–b).
evidence: This is based on distance measurements shown in Figure 5a-b.

claim: The Rab11-positive membranes are quite uniformly distributed around the ERC position at the membrane plane whatever the cell shape is.
source: Although the point that gives the most uniform angular distribution does not strictly coincide with the manually identified ERC, it is sufficiently close to indicate that the Rab11-positive membranes are quite uniformly distributed around the ERC position at the membrane plane whatever the cell shape is.
evidence: This is an inference from the uniformity analysis results.

claim: The ERC corresponds to the organizing hub of the Rab11 carrier vesicles.
source: This indicates that the ERC corresponds to the organizing hub of the Rab11 carrier vesicles.
evidence: This is an inference from the uniform distribution around the ERC.

claim: In untreated cells, the Euclidean distance between the reference point estimated at time t = 0 and the points estimated for the next frames remains stable.
source: In untreated cells, this distance remains stable (see Figure 6 green line).
evidence: This is based on data shown in Figure 6.

claim: The ERC location is moving away as Latrunculin A is affecting the cell.
source: We analyzed cells treated with Latrunculin A, which inhibits actin polymerization (see Appendix 1—figure 1 e–f). We show that the ERC location is moving away as the drug is affecting the cell (see Figure 6 blue and orange lines), enlightening the role of cytoskeleton in stabilizing the cellular localization of the ERC.
evidence: This is based on data shown in Figure 6.

claim: The cytoskeleton plays a role in stabilizing the cellular localization of the ERC.
source: We show that the ERC location is moving away as the drug is affecting the cell (see Figure 6 blue and orange lines), enlightening the role of cytoskeleton in stabilizing the cellular localization of the ERC.
evidence: This is an inference from the Latrunculin A treatment effects.

claim: The confinement ratio of Rab11 tracks is decreasing with time after Latrunculin A treatment.
source: The confinement ratio of Rab11 tracks is decreasing with time (see Figure 7), which is consistent with actin cytoskeleton being involved in Rab11 vesicle trafficking, as already reported (Schafer et al., 2014).
evidence: This is based on data shown in Figure 7.

claim: Actin cytoskeleton is involved in Rab11 vesicle trafficking.
source: The confinement ratio of Rab11 tracks is decreasing with time (see Figure 7), which is consistent with actin cytoskeleton being involved in Rab11 vesicle trafficking, as already reported (Schafer et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation and is consistent with the observed data.

claim: The radial distribution of Rab11 vesicles is constantly shifting from the cell periphery to the cell center for unconstrained, crossbow- and disk-shaped cells after Latrunculin A treatment.
source: The radial distribution of Rab11 vesicles is constantly shifting from the cell periphery to the cell center for unconstrained, crossbow- and disk-shaped cells (see Figure 8a).
evidence: This is based on data shown in Figure 8a.

claim: Before and at drug injection time, there are significant differences in radial distributions between the three tested conditions (p value = 0.0023).
source: However, before and at drug injection time, we observe significant differences in radial distributions between the three tested conditions (p value = 0.0023, see Figure 8b).
evidence: This is based on statistical analysis shown in Figure 8b.

claim: After Latrunculin A treatment, there is progressively no difference between the radial distributions as the actin organization is drastically perturbed.
source: After Latrunculin A treatment, we progressively observe no difference between the radial distributions, as the actin organization is drastically perturbed.
evidence: This is based on the analysis results and connects them to actin disruption.

claim: Exocytosis/recycling vesicle trafficking is dependent on both cell shape and actin organization.
source: Together, these quantifications allow us to conclude that exocytosis/recycling vesicle trafficking is dependent on both cell shape and actin organization.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the combined analysis of cell shape and Latrunculin A effects.

claim: QuantEv is publicly available.
source: In conclusion, QuantEv has the potential to become a very popular analysis method for dynamics and intracellular event analysis as (i) it is publicly available; (ii) it is fully automated and semi-parametric; (iii) it provides results that are easy to biologically interpret; (iv) it performs a statistical analysis that takes into account the biological variability over the replicated experiments of a same condition and is efficient with small and large amounts of data.
evidence: This is a statement about the software availability.

claim: QuantEv is fully automated and semi-parametric.
source: In conclusion, QuantEv has the potential to become a very popular analysis method for dynamics and intracellular event analysis as (i) it is publicly available; (ii) it is fully automated and semi-parametric; (iii) it provides results that are easy to biologically interpret; (iv) it performs a statistical analysis that takes into account the biological variability over the replicated experiments of a same condition and is efficient with small and large amounts of data.
evidence: This describes the technical characteristics of the method.

claim: The Rab6 proteins are extracted from each image sequence by using the C-CRAFT method with default parameters, except the p value that ranges from 0.0025 to 0.35 depending on the noise level.
source: The Rab6 proteins are extracted from each image sequence by using the C-CRAFT method (Pécot et al., 2015) with default parameters, except the p value that ranges from 0.0025 to 0.35 depending on the noise level, available on Icy (de Chaumont et al., 2012).
evidence: This describes the image analysis method used, with citations.

claim: The Rab11-positive membranes on micro-patterns are segmented at each time point with the ATLAS algorithm with default parameters, except the p value that ranges from 0.05 to 0.45 depending on the noise level.
source: The Rab11-positive membranes on micro-patterns are segmented at each time point with the ATLAS algorithm (Basset et al., 2015) with default parameters, except the p value that ranges from 0.05 to 0.45 depending on the noise level.
evidence: This describes the segmentation method used, with citation.

claim: A variance stabilization transform is performed to take into account the Poisson-Gaussian nature of the noise in the CCD sensors.
source: In both cases, a variance stabilization transform (Boulanger et al., 2010) is performed to take into account the Poisson-Gaussian nature of the noise in the CCD sensors.
evidence: This describes a preprocessing step with citation.

claim: Rab6 and Rab11 trajectories are estimated with the multiple hypothesis tracking method developed by Chenouard et al. (2013) with default parameters.
source: Finally, Rab6 and Rab11 trajectories are estimated with the multiple hypothesis tracking method developed by Chenouard et al. (2013) with default parameters, available on Icy (de Chaumont et al., 2012), the combinatorial optimization tracking method developed by Sbalzarini and Koumoutsakos (2005) with default parameters, available on ImageJ (Schneider et al., 2012) and the hybrid approach TrackMate (Tinevez et al., 2017) that first connects detected points into short tracks and then links the resulting tracks together, with default parameters, available on Fiji (Schindelin et al., 2012).
evidence: This describes the tracking methods used, with citations.

claim: Only the trajectories for which the gated distance is inferior to 2 pixels for at least two methods are used for the analysis.
source: Only the trajectories for which the gated distance is inferior to 2 pixels for at least two methods are used for the analysis.
evidence: This describes the quality control criterion for trajectory selection.

claim: A one-sided non-parametric Wilcoxon signed-rank test is used on the condition differences for all experiments to state if two conditions are statistically different.
source: For those two reasons, we propose to use the one-sided non-parametric Wilcoxon signed-rank test on the condition differences for all experiments to state if two conditions are statistically different.
evidence: This describes the statistical test used.

source: We also propose to use the bisection method to speed up the computation (about sixty times faster than the entropy map computation, see Appendix 5—table 1).
